data.narrative:
AlixLabs is a Series A chip-design company founded by Jonas Sundqvist, Dmitry Suyatin, and Amin Karimi, having raised €15M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor companies, including same-stage comparables SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix.

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the €15M raised as a proxy for post-money Series A value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage progression, implies a valuation of €30M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage companies yields a median valuation of €2.3B, with a range spanning €2.0B (d-Matrix) to €11.0B (SambaNova Systems). Public-comp anchoring via semiconductor P/S multiples (20.5x median across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue data. 

These methods produce a triangulated range of €26M (low) to €2.7B (high), with a median of €1.2B across two applicable methods. The extreme dispersion reflects material uncertainty around the peer set: SambaNova's €11B valuation represents a significant outlier, while d-Matrix and Rebellions cluster tighter near €2.0-2.3B. Stage-progression yields a conservative floor absent commercial traction data. Resolution of valuation dispersion requires clarity on AlixLabs' technology differentiation, IP position, and customer pipeline relative to named peers.
